newsitem.title: THAILAND: Siam City Bank delays FRCD issue.
newsitem.headline: Siam City Bank delays FRCD issue.

text.p: Siam City Bank Plc has delayed its issue of $100 million floating rate certificates of deposit because deposits are rising and it is awaiting the outcome of a Moody's review of Thai credit ratings, the lead arranger said.

"The new issue plan has been put on hold. The bank is watching now whether the increase in its deposits is going to be a stable phenomenon or not," Tony Li, managing director of primary markets at Chase Manhattan Asia, told Reuters.
Siam City Bank, acting through its Cayman Islands branch, had planned to launch the issue last month.
Li said that deposits had been rising significantly over the past few weeks as those who had withdrawn deposits from other weakened finance companies had switched deposits to Siam City.
"(The delay) is also because Thailand has been put on a credit watch (by Moody's)," he added.
Moody's Investors Service said last month it had placed the A2 foreign-currency sovereign ceilings for bonds and bank deposits of Thailand on review for possible downgrade.
Another rating agency, Standard & Poor's, on Tuesday affirmed Thailand's single-A long term and A-1 short-term foreign debt ratings.
Moody's early this month also said it may cut the debt, deposit and financial strength ratings of Siam City together with those of two other medium-sized banks.
"Moody's possible cut of Siam City's rating is just a second consideration (to delay the issue). The major consideration is the country's rating itself," Li said.
